Cue The Dice Davy Jones’ Dirge 🏴‍☠️
 ⚓ The sea is calling... and you're invited to witness the adventure.
 Step into the audience for Cue the Dice, Chattanooga Tabletop Revue's live-play Dungeons & Dragons series, where tabletop roleplaying becomes live theatre. Inspired by shows like Critical Role and Dimension 20, talented performers and community members gather around the stage to create an unforgettable story in real time—complete with dramatic roleplay, hilarious improvisation, unexpected twists, and the occasional catastrophic dice roll.
 In Davy Jones' Dirge, our adventurers set sail into cursed waters where ghost ships drift through the fog, forgotten treasures lure the greedy, and an ancient sea captain's mournful song echoes beneath the waves. Whether you're a longtime D&D fan or have never played a tabletop game, this is a unique theatrical experience that's easy to follow and incredibly fun to watch.

Katie’s enthusiasm and deep ecological knowledge brought these often‑overlooked creatures to life, highlighting not only their importance in local ecosystems but also the simple, meaningful ways we can garden for wildlife to support them. Our community left inspired and better equipped to create habitats that help these remarkable species thrive.

items.content_text: On Friday, our team at the Hamilton County Health Department partnered with WillowBend Farms, the Family Justice Center, Vision Hospitality Group, and community members at the Aloft Hotel for the Red Sand Project. This initiative raises awareness about human trafficking, a pressing issue that affects every community, including ours. By pouring red sand into sidewalk cracks, we show solidarity with survivors and highlight those who often fall through the cracks. Our department is committed to prevention, education, and supporting survivors. Thank you to everyone who joined us in sending the strong message that human trafficking has no place in Hamilton County. To learn more and access resources, visit health.hamiltonTN.org.

So thankful for another incredible evening at the 2026 Honoring The Sacrifice - American Heroes Dinner.
 This year was super special to me, having both kids there.  They’ve both attended separately, but having both of them there, together with me, was something I’ll never forget.
 Extremely humbling message delivered by Jason Redman, stressing the importance of the support and aid that Honoring the Sacrifice provides for our nations severely wounded veterans and their families.  Not only financially, but spiritually, sharing the love of Christ to all those they encounter and support.
 Each year that passes, these gatherings feel more like a family reunion.  I’m so thankful the Lord placed these people into my life, a little over 11 years ago.  I know for a fact, that I would not be the man I am today, and where I am today, without Him placing these precious people into my life.

Each year that passes, these gatherings feel more like a family reunion. I’m so thankful the Lord placed these people into my life, a little over 11 years ago. I know for a fact, that I would not be the man I am today, and where I am today, without Him placing these precious people into my life.

Sometimes the biggest takeaway from a day comes from the smallest moment.

Last week, members of our SETD team joined leaders from across the tri-state at Thrive Regional Partnership “Yes, And…” Summer Forum in South Pittsburg.

We toured the Lodge Cast Iron foundry and museum, saw firsthand the people and processes behind one of Southeast Tennessee’s most recognizable manufacturers, and joined conversations about transportation, infrastructure, community development, and what it takes to build a resilient future.

Along the way, one small moment stood out to us.

Inside the foundry, an employee has taken it upon himself to write a daily inspirational quote on a whiteboard for his coworkers. No one asked him to. He simply decided it was something he could do to encourage the people around him.

That day’s message: “A leader must inspire or his team will expire.”

It was a simple but meaningful reminder of something we see throughout our work at SETD: the strength of a region ultimately comes back to its people. The people who show up, share ideas, build things, collaborate, solve problems, encourage one another, and care about the communities they call home.

We’re grateful for Thrive Regional Partnership for creating opportunities like this.

 A Hixson family recently reported a paving scam to CPD. According to the family, a man claiming to work for Ace Asphalt and Paving came to their door and offered to pave their driveway. Remember, if you suspect you're the victim of a scam, alert your bank to freeze your account, file a report with your local law enforcement, and report the scam to the FTC.

Estonia’s economy is recovering from a severe and prolonged recession.
 The recovery is expected to continue despite higher energy prices, with GDP growing by 1.8% this year and 2.7% in 2027. Nevertheless, uncertainty remains high due to potential risks from energy prices and geopolitical tensions.
 The country enjoys a robust business environment, a resilient labour market and a sound fiscal framework. But sustaining the recovery and ensuring fiscal sustainability requires continuing spending reviews, rethinking taxation, managing the energy transition and addressing climate change.
 Estonia is a digital frontrunner, but AI adoption remains uneven across the economy. Expanding uptake in traditional sectors and strengthening AI skills will be key to boost productivity and growth.

I now have access to the city's social pages, Google account, YouTube, and the social media managers message thread across departments.

This spring, Dr. Ashleigh Pipes traveled to Shantou, China, where researchers from around the world came together to discuss the question, “How do people learn language?” 
 Pipes, an assistant professor in the UTC's Department of Applied Leadership and Learning, traveled to the International Association for the Psychology of Language Learning conference with support from a Professional Development Award from UTC’s Division of Access and Engagement. 
 “Attending this conference was undoubtedly the highlight of my academic year and provided opportunities for academic,professional and personal growth,” Pipes wrote in a summary of her experience. “PLL6 is a biannual conference that explores psychology in relation to language learning, applied to English as a second language as well as other foreign languages.” 
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/utc-faculty-member-presents-languag…/

items.title: Wowwwww!!! How about a midday blessing for a pick me up?!? Today I went to the CBMC(Christian Business Men’s Connection)...
items.content_text:
Wowwwww!!!
 How about a midday blessing for a pick me up?!? Today I went to the CBMC(Christian Business Men’s Connection) luncheon. The keynote speaker was Michael Bua.  And what a speaker he was! I left feeling not only invigorated and blessed,but also wanted to be a better Christ follower. Every year he buys two tickets. One for himself and gifts another. This year he gifted as his guest his son. Sitting at a table with his son,pastor,and fellow BNI family members it was truly wonderful. Mike spoke truths and strengths. He also spoke on his weaknesses throughout his life. Following the luncheon,I had this desire to give of myself. So I made a stop at the East Ridge Animal Services and gave some luvin’ to a pup. Cayenne and I played a bit and had a treat before I went to see a client. With the day starting with our Men’s Bible group and splashing in the luncheon later how could I not want to be a better version of myself. Thank you Michael for your insightful and inspiring speech today. Thank you to the pumped up pastor and brothers for starting the day off right!!💪🏻. Thank you Animal Services for all you do. Thank you Jesus for blessing me as you have.
 #blessed
 #luncheon
 #fellowship
 #CMBC

 Climate change is contributing to more severe wildfire conditions, with rising costs to people, health, biodiversity and economies. Governments are increasingly looking at ways to reduce wildfire risk, as well as emergency response measures. 
 #OECD analysis explores how countries can reduce wildfire risks    through prevention and long-term climate adaptation strategies.
